svg.title: SYN Mirror: why the NAT of the server lets the connection in
svg.text: A NAT lets in only answers: packets from the address its own computer sent to
the NAT of the server 198.51.100.7 · the meeting point 203.0.113.5, port 41933 · the NAT of the client 192.0.2.44

g.text: ③ The SYN of the server, out of its NAT

svg.text: its NAT notes: answers from 203.0.113.5:41933 come in

g.text: ④ The SYN of the client, at the meeting point

svg.text: the same port the server dials

g.text: ⑤ The same SYN, sent on to the server

svg.text: where the server's SYNs came from
exactly ③ reversed: for the NAT of the server it is the answer

g.text: ✓ The NAT of the server lets ⑤ in, and the server answers it: the connection is set up
✗ The SYN of the client as it was, from 192.0.2.44:31000, would be dropped: the server never sent there
